title: Streak Pricing 2026: Plans, Per-User Costs, Add-Ons
summary: Streak pricing runs $49 to $59 per user monthly depending on your billing cycle. Compare plan features and calculate your team's total cost.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces Fits a Streak Setup


Activepieces can send you a reminder before the seat count grows again, but it doesn't change what Streak charges and it doesn't replace Streak.


It's an MIT-licensed automation tool that connects the apps a team already uses across 746 integrations, and if an integration you need is missing, one can be generated with AI and added privately.


### Streak renewal and seat count reminders


Make the renewal date impossible to miss: that is the useful job here, and it is small. A renewal that nobody was watching is how a seat count from last spring gets billed again this year without anyone deciding it should.


Activepieces can run a scheduled flow that sends a reminder to whoever owns the budget, so the review happens while there's still time to change the number of seats.


A run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, and the free plan includes 1,000 credits a month, so the reminder adds no seat and no new line to the budget.


In the illustration below, which shows the shape of it, Streak's pipeline, with its deal cards, sits at the left; a spreadsheet and a calendar sit at the right.


One Activepieces flow links them, and a single arrow leads to a reminder dated 30 days before renewal.


The reminder is the point, and the rest is plumbing that feeds it. Whoever receives the reminder still has to do the checking: open the pricing page, count the people who actually log in, and decide.


After the illustration, the question is what the reminder should carry. A date alone is thin. Pair it with the current seat list, kept in the spreadsheet, so the person reading it can compare names against real use.


### Exporting Streak pipeline data to other tools


Pipeline data can also be moved out of Streak into a spreadsheet or another tool your team already uses, whether by an export or by a flow you build.


That matters for cost in one narrow way: if a contractor or part-time colleague only needs to see deal status, a shared sheet may serve them without a Streak seat.


Whether that's acceptable depends on your plan terms and on how current that person needs the data to be.


Flows are unlimited on every plan, free included, so the number of syncs you build doesn't change the bill. Then go back to the Streak side, where the actual decision gets made.
